text:
kevin: Heads-up: sample app after onboarding (post-install flow) shows dropped streaming responses on Android when using Retrofit + Flow adapter. Repro in app: start chat stream, after ~5s it fails with SocketTimeoutException despite client callTimeout longer. Anyone seen this?

maria: Which Retrofit / OkHttp versions? Also are you using per-call timeout via call.timeout() or client-level?

kevin: Retrofit 2.9.0, OkHttp 4.11.0, using a Flow call adapter (custom). Client callTimeout was 60s. I also tried call.timeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) on the Retrofit Call and it still cancels mid-stream.

ryan: Could be that the Flow adapter cancels the coroutine on backpressure. Newer OkHttp added per-call timeout but if the Call's ResponseBody source is being consumed slowly it can still throw.

samira: Quick question: are you enabling StrictMode or any dev VM policy in the post-install flow? That sometimes surfaces weird terminations for long-running streams.

kevin: No StrictMode. Runs on Dispatchers.IO. Logs show an OkHttp stack trace: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: timeout. No 401/refresh happening. Also noticed that after enabling R8 for the sample's debug variant (we recently flipped minifyEnabled on by mistake), the behavior regressed. Disabling minification stabilized the stream.

maria: That sounds like a ProGuard/R8 consumer rule problem. OkHttp uses internal classes for platform detection; if those get stripped you can end up with fallback codepaths that behave differently for timeouts. Add a consumer keep rule or don't minify the sample.

ryan: Another angle: Retrofit CallAdapter -> Flow implementations often wrap the call and cancel upstream when downstream closes. That cancellation interacts with OkHttp timeouts. But like you said, that wouldn't explain a premature SocketTimeoutException unless readTimeout is triggered.

kevin: Minimal repro from the sample app (snip):

```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .callTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(60))
  .readTimeout(Duration.ofSeconds(0)) // try 0 to disable read timeout
  .connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build()

interface Api {
  @GET("v1/stream")
  fun streamChat(): Flow<ResponseBody>
}

val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder()
  .baseUrl(BASE)
  .client(client)
  .addConverterFactory(ScalarsConverterFactory.create())
  .addCallAdapterFactory(FlowCallAdapterFactory()) // custom adapter
  .build()
```

kevin: Workaround that helped: pinning OkHttp to 4.10.0 or explicitly setting readTimeout(0) + callTimeout larger. Also disabling minification for debug build fixed it (so it's definitely an R8/proguard consumer-rule issue in the sample).

samira: For onboarding docs we should add a short note: "If you see mid-stream SocketTimeoutExceptions on Android, check proguard consumer rules and prefer explicit readTimeout(0) for long-lived streams. Avoid enabling minification in debug/post-install sample builds." I'll draft it.

maria: I can add a consumer proguard snippet to sample/gradle-config and a test that runs the stream on emulator API 31+. Also add a small doc blurb about per-call .timeout() vs client-level readTimeout vs callTimeout so engineers don't confuse them.

android-eng: FYI Android 14 changed some keepalive/idle TCP heuristics for background sockets; if your server expects long idle periods it might drop the connection and manifest as a socket timeout. We should add a compatibility note and link to internal ticket #3456.

kevin: Created a tiny PR with README updates and the debug minification fix. CC @samira for the sample app change. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/123 (draft). Thanks :thumbsup:

devex-bot: deploy-checklist: sample-app-updates branch has CI failures on unit tests (flaky emulator startup).

ryan: I'll dig into the CI flakes tomorrow, likely emulator cold start timing. For immediate onboarding, keep debug minify off and include the proguard note in the quickstart.

kevin: Great — thanks everyone. Leaving a short checklist in the PR: add proguard consumer keep, set readTimeout(0) in sample long-stream client, and a note in onboarding troubleshooting.
